newsitem.title: USA: CPI sees lower Q3 portrait studio sales.
newsitem.headline: CPI sees lower Q3 portrait studio sales.

text.p: CPI Corp said Friday that due to lower than expected third quarter portrait studio sales, it no longer expects that 1996 full year comparable earnings will exceed those of 1995.
Last year, CPI reported earnings from continuing operations of $1.26 a share and a loss from discontinued operations equal to $0.24 for a net income of $1.02.
CPI, which operates portrait studios in Sears, Roebuck and Co stores, said it had expected earnings for its fiscal year to end February 1, 1997 to exceed comparable earnings last year.

Those expectations depended on a strong second half including the fourth quarter. CPI said sales from its Sears Portrait Studio division should exceed last year's but not show a strength the company had expected.

CPI said it currently estimates third quarter portrait studio sales to be about $4 million lower than previously expected. This could reduce pre-tax portrait studio operating income about $2.5 million from prior estimates.

CPI said its fourth quarter is difficult to predict but these results and the trend suggest that full year comparable overall earnings are likely to be below last year's. The projection excludes effects of a photofinishing joint venture and pending share repurchases, it noted.
CPI reported sales last year of $527.6 million and operates more than 1,700 retail locations including 1,020 Sears studios.
